label: Alert fired
description: 5xx ratio breached the 5% threshold for 3 minutes and paged the payments on-call.

evidence.title: payment-api: HTTP 5xx ratio above 5% for 3m
evidence.detail: HTTP 503 rate increased from 0.4% to 31% over six minutes; checkout completion rate dropped from 99.1% to 68%. Monitor: http_5xx_ratio{service=payment-api,env=prod}. Runbook: runbooks.internal/payments/payment-api-5xx

evidence.title: payment-api v2.17.4 deployed 14 minutes before the alert
evidence.detail: Cart session cache: switch to per-worker connection pool, add billing-meta read to checkout path. Deployed by @m.okonkwo, rollout complete, 23 files changed, flagged high risk.

evidence.title: payment-api degraded; redis-cache and postgres-orders healthy
evidence.detail: payment-api status=degraded (critical service). redis-cache healthy, 1.2ms p95. postgres-orders healthy, 8.4ms p95. psp-acquirer-eu healthy, 210ms p95.

hint: Page just fired. Establish blast radius and whether anything changed before touching anything.

label: Cache pressure identified
description: Deeper evidence lands: RedisTimeout dominates the logs and the per-worker Redis pool is pinned at its maximum.

evidence.title: Redis client pool pinned at maximum (100/100) with 37 waiters
evidence.detail: payment-api holds max_connections=100 per worker against redis-cache; acquisition wait p95 742ms (baseline 3ms) and growing monotonically since 13:58.

evidence.title: Connection not released back to pool (checkout path)
evidence.detail: connection not released back to pool (checkout path) leak_canary=checkout_conn_leak open_connections=812

evidence.title: Redis node healthy: cpu 11%, used_memory 412MB, connected_clients 100
evidence.detail: redis-cache-3 reports healthy: ops/sec 18200, cpu 11%, used_memory 412MB, connected_clients=100. Redis CPU and latency are normal - the bottleneck is on the client side.

hint: The client side is the bottleneck. 'Redis CPU is normal' is expected here, not a reason to drop this hypothesis.

label: Restart mitigation applied
description: Only reachable by executing the restart action. Short-lived relief, no root-cause change.

evidence.title: After rolling restart: 5xx 31% -> 12% for ~45s, pool back to 58/100
evidence.detail: Workers restarted onto the same v2.17.4 build. Redis client pool recovered to 58/100 and 5xx fell to ~12%, then began climbing again as new connections leak.

hint: Symptom improved, cause untouched. Check whether the same build is still deployed before calling this a fix.

label: Regression after mitigation
description: Reachable after a temporary mitigation, or by advancing the simulation while the leak keeps leaking.

evidence.title: Incident returned to 31% 5xx within 48s of the restart
evidence.detail: RedisTimeout spiking again, pool active=100 max=100, same version v2.17.4 still deployed. The restart reset the symptom, not the cause.

hint: The mitigation expired. The failing condition is still deployed - roll back or fix the pool configuration.

label: Service recovered
description: Rollback applied, pool drained, 5xx back to baseline.

evidence.title: Resolved: 5xx 0.4%, checkout 99.3%, redis pool 63/100
evidence.detail: payment-api rolled back to v2.17.3. Redis client pool drained to 63/100, pool wait 3ms, checkout success recovered to 99.3%.

hint: Stable at baseline for 5 minutes. Time to write the postmortem and retain the lessons.
